key_insight: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA) is a model-agnostic orchestration layer that separates oncology data routing from AI inference to make multimodal decision support more scalable and flexible.
clinical_relevance: If adopted, this architecture could help hospitals integrate changing AI models without rebuilding the whole clinical workflow, supporting more modular cancer decision support systems.
method: Formalized the system as a 7-tuple architecture with “Algorithmic Impermeability” to keep orchestration independent of the AI model.
Introduced an “Entry Theory” using Geometric Deep Learning to standardize multimodal patient data across structural and medical dimensions.
Used a Cancer Switching Module and a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP) to route data and isolate AI execution from hospital IT variability.
evidence_signal: In a proof-of-concept, the framework was tested across four technical scenarios and showed negligible orchestration overhead, invariant routing during model swaps, and 100% recall for targeted supplementary data requests under injected anomalies.
watch_item: The evidence is limited to a technical proof-of-concept, so real-world clinical integration, workflow fit, and interoperability with live EMR systems still need validation.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
